Rashi on Chullin 73a:13:1.hebrew: ואת האבר המדולדל בה - בשום בהמה שנחתך ממנו אבר ומעורה ותלוי במקצת, דאמרי' בהעור והרוטב (לקמן חולין דף קכז:): האבר המדולדל בבהמה ונשחטה — מטמאה טומאת אוכלין ולא טומאת נבלות, מדקתני "הוכשרו בדמיה", ואי נבלה — מאי הכשר איכא למימר? ואע"פ שאסורין באכילה, כדקתני לקמן בשמעתין: "להביא האבר והבשר המדולדלים":
Rashi on Chullin 73a:13:1.english: And the limb that hangs from it - [This refers to] any animal from which a limb was severed, yet remains attached and partially hanging, as we say in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev (later, Chullin 127b): A limb that hangs from an animal, and [the animal] was slaughtered, imparts the impurity of foods and not the impurity of carcasses — since [the Mishnah] teaches: "They are rendered susceptible [to impurity] through its blood," and if [it were] a carcass, what susceptibility could be said [to apply]? [This is so] even though they are prohibited for consumption, as [is] taught later in our sugya: "to include the dangling limb and flesh."

Rashi on Chullin 73a:13:2.hebrew: דבר שגופה - כלומר, דין הוא שתטהרנו, שהיא גופה:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:13:2.english: Something that is [part of] its own body - That is to say, it is logical that [slaughter] should render it pure, since it is [part of] its own body:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:15:1.english: Just as [there is] a dispute - [meaning] regarding a limb of fetuses:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:15:2.hebrew: כך מחלוקת באבר - המדולדל בבהמה, דלרבי מאיר אין שחיטתו מטהרתו, ולרבנן שחיטתו מטהרתו:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:15:2.english: So [too is] a dispute regarding a limb - that is dangling from an animal: for according to Rabbi Meir, its slaughter does not render it pure [from carcass impurity], whereas according to the Rabbis, its slaughter does render it pure:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:16:1.hebrew: עושה ניפול - בשעת שחיטה, הרי הוא כנופל ממנה ואין שחיטתו מועלת לו. ומשום לישנא דקרא, דילפינן לקמן "מיתה עושה ניפול", נקט לה:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:16:1.english: Renders [it] as fallen - At the time of slaughter, it [the limb] is as though it had fallen off from it [the animal], and its slaughter is of no avail for it. And [the Gemara] used this [phrasing] because of the wording of the verse, from which we derive below [that] "death renders [it] as fallen":

Rashi on Chullin 73a:17:1.hebrew: אליבא דרבנן - דבאבר דעובר מטהרי, ובאבר המדולדל בה מטמאין:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:17:1.english: According to the Rabbis - for regarding the limb of a fetus they render [it] pure, whereas regarding a limb dangling from it [the animal] they render [it] impure:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:17:2.hebrew: בחזרה - כדאמר ר' יוחנן בריש פירקין (לעיל חולין דף סח:): אבר עצמו מותר באכילה אם החזיר:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:17:2.english: By returning - As Rabbi Yochanan said at the beginning of our chapter (above, Chullin 68b): the limb itself is permitted to be eaten if [the fetus] returned [it into the womb]:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:1:1.english: [It] is as though [it were] cut - and thus they [the foreleg and the fetus] are touching one another:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:2:1.hebrew: עד מקום מדה - שהוא עתיד לקיים, ומה שעתיד לקוץ אין צריך טבילה, דכקצוץ דמי:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:2:1.english: Until the point of [its] measure - that he intends to retain; and that which he intends to cut off does not require immersion, as it is regarded as [already] cut off:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:4:1.hebrew: חבורי אוכלין - שהן רכין, אינו חשיב חבור, וכמאן דמיפרתי דמו. ודאמרינן בעלמא (פסחים דף פה.) לרבינא "חבורי אוכלין כמאן דמיפרתי דמו", מהכא נפקא:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:4:1.english: Connections of food - [since] they are soft, it is not considered a connection, and they are [considered] as though separated. And that which we say elsewhere (Pesachim 85a) according to Ravina, "connections of food are [considered] as though separated," is derived from here:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:5:1.english: Granted, according to Ulla - who says the reason is because of separation:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:5:2.hebrew: היינו דקתני - מתני' חתכו, דאי לא חתכו אין טמא, משום דמגע סתרים הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:5:2.english: This is what [it] teaches - [in] the Mishnah: "he severed it" — for if he did not sever it, it is not impure, because it is concealed contact:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:5:3.hebrew: איידי דתנא רישא חתכו - ואחר כך שחט את אמו, הבשר טהור; דדוקא חתכו קודם שחיטה, דמשעה שנשחטה ונראית לטומאת אוכלין לא נגע, הא לא חתכו, טמא:
Rashi on Chullin 73a:5:3.english: Since [the Mishnah] taught in the first clause, "[If] he severed it - and afterward slaughtered its mother, the meat is pure": [there it needed to specify "severed it"] because specifically [when] he severed it before slaughter [is the meat pure], since from the moment [the mother] was slaughtered and became fit for food impurity, [the meat] did not touch [the severed limb]; whereas [if] he did not sever it, it is impure:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:5:4.english: [The mishna] taught [in] the latter clause: "he severed it" - And even without severing it, the fetus is also impure:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:6:1.english: Does it impart impurity? - [The Gemara asks this] because [the Mishnah] teaches regarding it the law of contact [impurity]:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:6:2.english: [It] imparts impurity to consecrated [items] - by rabbinic decree:

Rashi on Chullin 73a:9:1.english: They said to him: It shields much [more], etc. - Further on, [the Gemara] explains what they are answering him:

Tosafot on Chullin 73a:2:1.hebrew: מטביל עד מקום מדה - ואם תאמר: ואידך ליהוי חציצה, דהוי מיעוטו המקפיד, דמיעוטו המקפיד חוצץ בכלים כמו באדם, כדמשמע במסכת מקואות (פ"ט מ"ז)! ויש לומר: דאיירי בידות הכלים העשויין כעין חוליות, כאותן שלשלאות של ברזל העשויין בטבעות. והא דקתני נמי סיפא במסכת מקואות (פ"י מ"ה): "שלשלת דלי גדול ארבעה טפחים, ושל קטן עשרה טפחים, ומטביל עד מקום מדה; ר' טרפון אומר: עד שיטבול כל הטבעת", מכלל דת"ק לא בעי כל הטבעת — מיירי נמי כגון דאותה טבעת עצמה עשויה כחוליות מטבעות קטנות, וליכא חציצה:
Tosafot on Chullin 73a:2:1.english: One immerses [them] until the point of [their eventual] size - And if you will say: But let the other [part of the handle] be an interposition, since it is a minority [of the vessel] about which one is particular — for a minority about which one is particular interposes in vessels just as in a person, as is implied in tractate Mikvaot (9:7)! One can say: [The Mishnah] is speaking of handles of vessels that are made like links, like those iron chains that are made of rings. And as for that which it also teaches in the latter clause in tractate Mikvaot (10:5): "The chain of a large bucket [must be immersed to] four handbreadths, and of a small [bucket to] ten handbreadths, and one immerses until the point of [its] measure; Rabbi Tarfon says: Until he immerses the entire ring" — from which it follows that the first Tanna does not require [immersing] the entire ring — [that] also speaks of a case where that ring itself is made like links of small rings, so there is no interposition:

Tosafot on Chullin 73a:4:1.hebrew: חבורי אוכלים כמאן דמפרתי דמו - תימה דלא משני הכי בהעור והרוטב (לקמן חולין דף קכח:) גבי "חישב עליו ואח"כ חתכו, טמא", ופריך: טומאת בית הסתרים הוא, ודוחק להעמידה כר' מאיר! וי"ל, דלא אמרינן "כמאן דמפרתי דמו" אלא היכא דעומד ליקצץ, כמו הכא, דאבר אסור והשאר מותר; וכן בסוף כיצד צולין (פסחים דף פה.) גבי "אבר שיצא מקצתו", דמה שיצא אסור ומה שבפנים מותר. אבל גבי אבר מן החי, דהכל אסור ואין עומד ליחתך, לא אמרינן כמאן דמיפרתי דמו:
Tosafot on Chullin 73a:4:1.english: Connections of foods are considered as though they are separated - It is astonishing that [the Gemara] does not answer thus in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev (later, Chullin 128b) regarding [the case where] "one thought about it [to eat it] and afterward cut it off, [that] it is impure," where [the Gemara] asks: It is a concealed impurity, and it is forced to establish it according to Rabbi Meir! And one can answer that we only say "considered as though they are separated" where it stands to be cut off, like here, where the [dangling] limb is forbidden and the rest is permitted; and similarly at the end of [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (Pesachim 85a), regarding "a limb part of which went outside," where that which went outside is forbidden and that which is inside is permitted. However, regarding a limb from a living animal, where the entire [animal] is forbidden and it does not stand to be cut off, we do not say "considered as though they are separated":
